item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 282316
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Wed Oct 28 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on recently
downgraded Tropical Depression Vance, located a couple hundred miles
west of Cabo Corrientes, Mexico.

Well Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
A broad area of low pressure could develop well to the southeast of
the Hawaiian Islands by this weekend or early next week. Thereafter,
environmental conditions appear generally favorable for some slow
development of this system as it moves westward to
west-northwestward into the Central Pacific basin.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Tropical Depression Vance Public Advisory Number 31
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Wed Oct 28 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 290232
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Vance Advisory Number  31
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
800 PM MST Wed Oct 28 2026
 
...SHOWER AND THUNDERSTORM ACTIVITY REDEVELOPS NEAR VANCE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM MST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...21.1N 108.1W
ABOUT 285 MI...460 KM WNW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 160 MI...260 KM WNW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNE OR 25 DEGREES AT 13 MPH...20 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests along the west-central and northwestern coasts of Mexico
and the southern Baja California Peninsula should monitor the
progress of Vance.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM MST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Vance
was located near latitude 21.1 North, longitude 108.1 West. The
depression is moving toward the north-northeast near 13 mph (20
km/h). A turn to the north, followed by a decrease in forward
speed, is expected over the next 24 hours.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Slight weakening is forecast to occur during the next day or so, and
Vance is expected to become post-tropical within the next 24 hours,
dissipating shortly thereafter.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches). 
Recently there was a ocean drifter buoy that reported a minimum 
pressure of 1002 mb (29.59 inches) as Vance moved over its 
location. 
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
RAINFALL: Through Thursday, Vance is expected to produce 2 to 4
inches of rain across central and southern Sinaloa, far southwestern
Durango, and far northwestern Nayarit, with isolated higher totals
of 7 inches possible over central and southern Sinaloa. This
rainfall may produce flooding and mudslides, especially in areas
along steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Vance,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Vance will affect coastal portions of
southwestern and west-central Mexico, as well as the southern
portion of the Baja California Peninsula during the next couple of
days. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Papin
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Depression Vance Forecast Discussion Number 31
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Wed Oct 28 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 290233
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Depression Vance Discussion Number  31
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
800 PM MST Wed Oct 28 2026

As anticipated, Vance's deep convection has re-ignited this evening, 
with cloud top temperatures as cold as -80 degrees C. This 
convective activity has pulled at the storm's center of circulation 
as well, with earlier visible satellite imagery showing the center 
briefly becoming obscured. TAFB's subjective Dvorak intensity 
estimate remains at a 2.0 for a final T number, with objective 
estimates from UW-CIMSS ranging from 27-36 kt. Based on these data, 
Vance's initial intensity is held steady at 30 kt, though its 
possible higher gusts could be present within the deep convection.

With this convective redevelopment, Vance has turned to the 
north-northeast with a somewhat faster forward motion, estimated at 
025/11 kt. Vance is being steered by a broad trough centered over 
the eastern Pacific, and is expected to turn back to the north once 
convection wanes on Thursday. The latest NHC track forecast reflects 
largely a blend of the HCCA and TVCN models, and is a little east of 
the previous track, partially due to adjustments in the initial 
position. 

Strong vertical wind shear will continue to erode Vance's core over 
the next 24 hours. Simulated satellite imagery from the GFS and 
ECMWF suggests that the ongoing convection, expected to last most of 
overnight, will be Vance's last gasp before it is fully sheared off, 
leading to the cyclone becoming a post-tropical remnant low during 
the latter half of tomorrow. Vance is then expected to dissipate 
shortly thereafter as it interacts with mountainous terrain along 
the western Mexican coastline. The latest NHC intensity forecast 
depicts slight weakening after Vance's convective max tonight, 
before weakening into a post-tropical remnant low by tomorrow 
evening.
 

Key Message:

1. Periods of heavy rainfall associated with Vance will impact 
portions of western Mexico during much of this week. This rainfall 
may produce flooding and mudslides across central and southern 
Sinaloa, far southwestern Durango, and far northwestern Nayarit, 
especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  29/0300Z 21.1N 108.1W   30 KT  35 MPH
 12H  29/1200Z 22.2N 107.6W   30 KT  35 MPH
 24H  30/0000Z 23.7N 107.7W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 36H  30/1200Z 25.2N 108.1W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 48H  31/0000Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Papin
